From 356b57752c91cffb35356abe6647065bf0edcad1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Rafael J. Wysocki" <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Feb 2018 12:10:59 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
index d1a01311c1a2..5e3df194723e 100644
--- a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
+++ b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
@@ -376,6 +376,7 @@ static int intel_hid_remove(struct platform_device *device)
 {
 	acpi_handle handle = ACPI_HANDLE(&device->dev);
 
+	device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
 	acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
 	intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
 	intel_button_array_enable(&device->dev, false);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c`**
- A new line was added in the `intel_hid_remove` function: `device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);`. This line resets the wakeup capable flag for the intel-hid device when it is removed.

### Relationships
The modification ensures that when the intel-hid device is removed, it correctly updates its sysfs attributes to indicate that it can no longer wake up the system. This change is necessary because the device's ability to wake the system is dependent on the presence of its notify handler, which is removed during the device's removal process. The patch addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (ef884112e55c) that allowed the device to wake the system even after it was no longer capable of doing so.

Here is the commit message:
platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the intel-hid device retains its wakeup capability in the system's attributes even after the notify handler is removed, leading to incorrect behavior where the device is still reported as able to wake the system despite being removed. This inconsistency arises from not resetting the wakeup capable flag when the device is removed.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int intel_hid_remove(struct platform_device *device)
 {
 	acpi_handle handle = ACPI_HANDLE(&device->dev);
 
+	device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
 	acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
 	intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
 	intel_button_array_enable(&device->dev, false);
 
 	/*
 	 * Even if we failed to shut off the event stream, we can still
 	 * safely detach from the device.
 	 */
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
```
```c
// Wakeup capability flag is not reset here
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `acpi_remove_notify_handler` function removes the notify handler for the intel-hid device, but the wakeup capability flag is not reset. As a result, the device continues to be reported as capable of waking the system, leading to incorrect behavior after the device has been removed.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
```
Reason:
This statement resets the wakeup capability flag for the intel-hid device to `false` when the device is removed. By doing this, it ensures that the system attributes accurately reflect the device's inability to wake the system, thus fixing the inconsistency that caused the bug.
